summary: Tested RISEDUALAI Bearer token auth and AI hypothesis features. Backend APIs (15 tests) all pass. Frontend login flow blocked by intermittent 502 errors from infrastructure (ingress/load balancer).

integration_issues.issue: Intermittent 502 errors from infrastructure cause login requests to hang. The backend responds correctly (verified via curl), but browser requests often get 502 from ingress/load balancer.
integration_issues.root_cause: Infrastructure issue - ingress/load balancer returning 502 errors intermittently. Backend is healthy and responding correctly.
integration_issues.evidence: curl tests pass consistently, but browser fetch gets 502 ~50% of the time

integration_issues.flow: Auth state restoration on page reload
integration_issues.issue: When tokens are in localStorage but /api/auth/me fails with 502, user state is set to false (logged out) even though tokens are valid
integration_issues.suggestion: Add retry logic to checkAuth function in AuthContext.jsx for transient errors

action_items: CRITICAL: Investigate infrastructure 502 errors - ingress/load balancer is intermittently failing requests
MEDIUM: Add retry logic to AuthContext.jsx checkAuth function for transient 502 errors
LOW: Consider adding a loading timeout with error message in AuthModal when request takes >10 seconds
critical_code_review_comments: Auth implementation is correct - Bearer tokens in localStorage, Authorization header sent correctly
Hypothesis paywall logic is correct - free users get teaser (is_pro=false), pro users get full analysis (is_pro=true)
CORS is correctly configured with allow_origins=['*'] which works with Bearer tokens (no credentials needed)
AuthContext.jsx could benefit from retry logic for transient errors in checkAuth function
seed_data_creation: Admin user auto-seeded on startup with idempotent logic
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend auth and hypothesis APIs work correctly (verified via pytest - 15/15 tests pass). Frontend integration blocked by intermittent 502 errors from infrastructure. The Bearer token auth implementation is correct - tokens are returned in response body, stored in localStorage, and sent via Authorization header. The issue is infrastructure-level, not code-level.

TestAuthLogin: test_login_admin_success - PASSED (returns access_token, refresh_token, role=admin, subscription=pro)
TestAuthMe: test_me_with_valid_token - PASSED (returns user info with Bearer token)

AuthModal: Login button visible in navbar - PASSED
Login form submission - BLOCKED (502 errors from infrastructure)
Direct fetch test: Direct fetch from browser console - INTERMITTENT (works after retries, fails ~50% of time with 502)

mocked_apis.note: Alpaca broker trading endpoints are mocked. All auth, hypothesis, and scraping endpoints use REAL data.

rca_of_the_issue.details: The backend is healthy and responding correctly to all requests (verified via curl and pytest). However, browser requests through the ingress/load balancer get 502 errors approximately 50% of the time. This causes the login form to hang on 'Please wait...' indefinitely.
evidence: curl tests pass consistently (100% success rate)
Browser console shows 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 502'
Direct fetch from browser console works after 1-2 retries
mitigation: Short-term: Add retry logic to frontend fetch calls
Long-term: Investigate and fix infrastructure 502 errors
